pull.title: fix(pr-checkpoint): press /pathway from any session, no new session per PR worktree
pull.body:
/pathway and the pr_checkpoint tool ran the checkpoint engine in the session root. For a PR whose branch lives in another worktree, Dave had to start a new Claude session inside that worktree before he could press /pathway. Now the mod finds the worktree that has the PR branch checked out and runs there, so /pathway works from any CCv3 session.

## What changed

- **pr-checkpoint/model.ts:** `gh pr view` also reads `headRefName`. New `worktreeFor(porcelain, branch)` reads `git worktree list --porcelain` and returns the worktree that has the branch checked out.
- **pr-checkpoint/index.tsx:** `prepare()` picks the checkout:
  - the worktree that holds the PR branch, when it has the engine;
  - else the session root (the old behaviour).
  The engine `--json`, the pre-pr stamp, the git facts and both presses (`--confirm`, `--apply`) run in that checkout. A relative body path resolves in the checkout first, then in the session root. A head mismatch now names the branch and the checkout.
- Headless runs and non-composer origins are unchanged: the text plan in the session root, no gh call.
- **README:** the checkpoint row describes the lookup.

## Evidence

Proof type: bugfix

RED: `claude plugin test .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods` @ 6d77dacc (this branch's test file against main's sources)
```text
(fail) W1 the engine, the stamp and the git facts run in the worktree that holds the PR branch
(fail) W2 a press runs --confirm and --apply in the worktree, with the body file resolved there
(fail) W3 a body file that only the session root holds is still found there
(fail) W5 /pathway <pr> none --body from the main checkout records in the worktree
(fail) W6 no worktree holds the PR branch and the session root is elsewhere: the refusal names the branch
 1037 pass
 5 fail
```

GREEN: `claude plugin test .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods` @ c1911761
```text
 1045 pass
 0 fail
tsc --noEmit -p .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods/tsconfig.json: exit 0
claude plugin validate .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods: Validation passed
node --test scripts/mods/validate-mods.test.mjs: pass 11, fail 0
live: worktreeFor on this machine's git worktree list: fix/pathway-session-root -> .claude/worktrees/pathway-root, main -> C:/Users/dkhay/continuous-claude, no/such-branch -> null
live: gh pr view 227 --json ...,headRefName: headRefName fix/review-merge-gate
```

Artifacts: `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-pathway-root-red.txt`, `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-pathway-root-green.txt`, `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-pathway-root-live-worktree.txt`.

## Reviews before this PR opened

- pre-pr CodeRabbit CLI on deec5122: 1 Minor (the tool text said a headless run reads a worktree-relative body), fixed in c1911761.
- Opus review of the build: 0 Major, 3 Minor, 3 Nit; all fixed before the commit:
  - Lock B read HEAD in the session root; the record now stores its checkout and Lock B reads HEAD there (W8; it fails with the old cwd).
  - The engine code came from the PR worktree; it now always comes from the session root, with the worktree as cwd only.
  - The decoy branch in the W1 fixture came after the real one; it now comes first, with CRLF line ends and a detached block.
  - Windows path compare, a missing-body text that named one path of two, and no test for a failing worktree list (W7, W9).

## Scope not included

- The pane press itself needs Dave: this PR's own /pathway press, from the main checkout session, is the live end-to-end check.

Model + harness: claude-opus-5-5 (orchestration, Opus review) via Claude Code.

https://claude.ai/code/session_0162xu8GPKraAf3vEmY7PuV8

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Checkpoints now use the checkout associated with the pull request’s branch when available, including when that branch is in a separate worktree.
  * Body files are searched for in the pull request checkout first, with fallback to the session checkout. Headless mode continues to search only the session checkout.
  * When the checkpoint engine is unavailable in the pull request checkout, execution falls back to the session checkout.
  * Checkpoint validation now checks the pull request checkout’s current revision.

app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).
